titulo: That 'package problem' text is a scam
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que casi cae en un texto falso de paquete a su amigo que toca todos los links, para decirle que no use el link y que reenvíe el texto al 7726
regla_guardable: Surprise package text? Don't tap. Forward it to 7726.
fuentes: FTC Consumer Alert, April 23, 2025: Think that text message is from USPS? It could be a scam (texts claim unpaid postage, a missed delivery or a shipping update; the link leads to a look-alike of a real website that asks for personal or financial information; don't click, check tracking through the retailer or account where you ordered; report in the messaging app or forward to 7726; ReportFraud.ftc.gov)

frases.texto: Your phone says a package is stuck, and you tap the link to fix it.
That's exactly what the scammer wants.
The FTC says these texts claim unpaid postage, a missed delivery, or a shipping update.
The link leads to a look-alike of a real website, where you're told to enter personal or financial information.
Heads up: a real package might be on its way. Just don't use the link in the text.
Instead, check tracking through the store where you ordered.
Then report the text in your messaging app, or forward it to seven seven two six.
Send this to the friend who taps every link.
